video.title: The Magic of Single-Foot Forehand Training

classification.reason: The coach and a demonstrator analyze reps of single-foot forehand probing to teach proper foot loading, visual probing, and body adjustments.

problem.title_as_question: How does single-foot probing training fix forehand foot loading and spacing issues?
problem.definition: Players often fail to run deep enough into the forehand corner to get their loading foot behind the ball, causing reaching arm swings without weight transfer, and lack the probing precision and body adaptability to handle imperfect spacing.
prerequisites: open or semi-open stance forehand fundamentals

symptoms.description: The player reaches with their arm and curls around the ball rather than driving forward through the court.
There is no weight transfer from the loading foot through the body into the shot.
The shot feels unsolid and lacks clean power when reaching and curling with the arm.
The player's upper body leans or adjusts erratically to compensate for improper ball spacing.

causes.statement: The loading foot is not positioned behind the ball and therefore cannot press forward through the court.
The player does not move deep enough into the forehand corner to set the loading foot behind the shot.
The player has insufficient visual tracking and probing ability to accurately position the body in its optimal contact zone.
The player attempts to execute an identical swing when poorly probed instead of dynamically adapting body posture to the ball.

angles.summary: Setting the loading foot behind the ball and deep in the corner enables the foot to press through the court, naturally transferring body weight through the shot.
Alexa consistently probes into the most comfortable spot so her swing remains repeatable, whereas the coach misjudges spacing and must lean or throw his racket overhead to compensate.
Players wrongly take the exact same arm swing on every shot and miss when spacing is off, rather than tracking the ball with their eyes and using body adjustments to preserve the hitting zone.
Failing to position the loading foot behind the ball forces an arm curl around the ball that never feels solid or good.

solutions.summary: Hop and probe the ball on one foot to hit forehands, creating a punishing training stimulus that demands sharp visual tracking and precise loading foot positioning.
solutions.external_goal: Get the loading foot deep into the corner and behind the ball, then press it back through the court towards the target.

solutions.summary: Look at the ball, swing through the ball you see, and adjust body posture as needed so your swing through the contact zone stays consistent.
Observe whether the lower body sets in a balanced position from which weight transfers naturally into the shot, or if you are reaching and curling with the arm.
